transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I've been struggling a lot lately with actually finishing tasks, like my schoolwork or chores around the house, even after I start them. I also find myself constantly avoiding or putting off anything that requires a lot of mental focus because it just feels too overwhelming.
Have you been feeling sad, empty, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, or have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?
No, I haven't been feeling sad, empty, or hopeless. I still really enjoy my usual hobbies and activities, so I don't think I've lost interest in those things.

I haven't really been feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, and I definitely haven't lost interest in my usual activities. I still want to do them, but I just struggle to stay focused on them if they require a lot of mental effort.
Do you often find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things, even when there's no apparent reason to worry, or do you feel anxious about a wide range of things for more days than not?
No, I don't really struggle with excessive worrying or constant anxiety about everyday things. I feel pretty calm most of the time, so anxiety isn't really an issue for me.

Can you tell me more about what happens when you try to focus on tasks that require a lot of mental effort - do you find your mind wandering, have trouble following instructions, or get easily distracted by your surroundings?

I actively avoid tasks that require a lot of mental effort because they feel too overwhelming to even start. When I do try to do them, I have a really hard time following instructions, which means I rarely finish my chores or schoolwork. I'm not really sure about my mind wandering or getting distracted, but the main issue is just not being able to follow through.
Have you experienced any changes in your motivation or interest in activities, or do you feel like you're just going through the motions, even if you're not feeling sad or hopeless?

I haven't really noticed a general loss of interest, and I don't feel like I'm just going through the motions. I'm not really sure how to answer that, as my main struggle is just with the effort needed to actually do my tasks.
How do you think your difficulties with focusing and completing tasks have affected your daily life, such as your relationships, work, or school performance?

These difficulties have a huge impact on my daily life, especially since I often fail to finish my schoolwork, chores, and work duties because I struggle to follow through on instructions. I also tend to avoid or delay any tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort, which has been causing serious issues with my school performance.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with focusing and completing tasks, and have you always had trouble with them or did they start at some point in your life?

I've been experiencing these specific difficulties for about 7 months now. However, I have actually had similar struggles with focus and completing tasks since childhood, definitely before I turned 12.
Did you have any accommodations or support in school due to your difficulties with focus and task completion, such as an Individualized Education Program (IEP) or a 504 plan?
I don't recall having any official accommodations or support plans like an IEP or a 504 plan during school. I think I just tried to get through it on my own, even though it was really difficult.

Just to summarize, you've had lifelong difficulties with focusing and completing tasks, which have significantly impacted your daily life, particularly in school, and you've managed without formal accommodations, is that correct?

Yes, that's exactly right. I've struggled with following instructions, finishing schoolwork or chores, and avoiding mentally demanding tasks since before I was 12, and it's been a constant issue for at least the last 7 months. I have just had to manage these lifelong difficulties on my own without any formal accommodations.
